messages:
sam_sales: Heads-up — ClearPay asked us to onboard an open model called sylvan-2-13b and pin a specific commit/hash for their EU deployment. They also want a cheaper quantized variant as a fallback. Can product confirm feasibility and rough ETA?
anya: Thanks Sam. Do we have the exact model artifact (hf link or tarball) + the commit/hash they want pinned? Also confirm region constraint: EU-only or EU-primary with global fallback?
sam_sales: They shared an HF repo link in the email: 
https://huggingface.co/clearpay/sylvan-2-13b (they want commit f3a1c9 pinned). EU-primary — must serve from EU regions, but permitted to failover to US for <5% of requests when capacity is saturated.
anya: Got it. Priority: looks like mid-sales (pilot). I'll do a quick triage. Marc & Neha, can you check model architecture/compat issues (KV cache size, 13B memory profile) and whether we have a validated quantization recipe that preserves their perf?
marc_eng: Quick notes: sylvan-2 looks like standard decoder-only with some custom rotary embedding tweaks. Might need a small kernel tweak for our CUDA kernels (rotary param mismatch). Memory wise 13B in fp16 is fine on 80GB A100 but latency profile depends on context window. What quantization target? int8? int4?
neha_ml: We ran initial eval a while back on a similar model family. int8 dynamic works but int4 needs per-layer calibration to keep quality. If they accept a 2–3% generation-quality delta, int4 is possible. Need an eval prompt set from ClearPay to validate.
liam_infra: Capacity note: EU pools are ~85% booked next quarter. Can host but would need either dedicated slots (reserved) or autoscale burst to other EU zones; fallback to US is doable but requires routing policy and customer consent for data residency (they said allowed for <5%).
ricardo_devex: From an integration standpoint we can support version pinning via catalog entry + model_version field. Example config: ```
model: clearpay/sylvan-2-13b
version: f3a1c9
region_policy:
  primary: eu-west-1
  fallback: us-east-1
fallback_threshold_pct: 5
quant_profiles:
  - name: sylvan-2-int8
    quant: int8_dynamic
```
elaine_support: Also flagging SSO/KMS requirement — ClearPay requires keys stay in EU KMS. For Private/Dedicated customers that changes onboarding flow. Do they have Private deployment or Hosted?
sam_sales: Pilot will be on Hosted but customer expects contractual language around EU data residency + opt-in for US fallback. No Private deployment for pilot.
anya: Two key tracks then: 1) Catalog onboarding + pinned version + routing policy; 2) Quantized fallback + quality gate. Acceptance criteria proposal: 
- Model appears in catalog with version f3a1c9 and EU-primary routing
- 95th percentile latency <= 450ms for their typical prompt set at 8 concurrent RPS (we need their prompt set)
- Quantized variant (int8) passes customer prompt QA: top-line metrics (perplexity delta < 3%, manual QA pass)
- Documented fallback behavior + explicit opt-in recorded in contract
If those are met, we can greenlight pilot.
marc_eng: Technical checklist: 
- Kernel patch for rotary embedding compat (small change)
- End-to-end smoke on eu-west (fp16)
- Bench int8 using our quant pipeline and run perf/regression tests
I'll need ~3 dev-days to land the kernel and smoke.
neha_ml: I'll coordinate evals once they share prompt set. Estimate 2–4 days for calibration and report.
liam_infra: For capacity, suggest we offer a short-term reserved pool for pilot (1–2 weeks) or we accept EU-primary with explicit US fallback policy. Reserved pool reduces failure risk and simplifies SLA. Need ops signoff for 1–2 weeks of reservations.
ricardo_devex: Devdocs task: add example for version pin and routing config + sample SDK call. I can draft a PR once product confirms fields.
anya: Scope negotiation: Sales wants quick pilot; engineering needs kernel + eval; infra needs capacity commitments. Proposal: put this in product backlog as P2 with an accelerated pilot lane if legal signs data residency fallback clause. Timeline if approved today: 
- Day 0–1: get prompt set + artifact (sam)
- Day 1–4: kernel + smoke (marc)
- Day 2–5: quant calibration + QA (neha)
- Day 3–6: infra reserve + routing config + devdocs (liam/ricardo)
- Day 6–8: customer QA + pilot go/no-go (all)
That is optimistic — realistic is 10 business days to full pilot.
sam_sales: I'll push legal to accept explicit fallback clause and share prompt set today. Can we get a one-page checklist we can send to ClearPay?
anya: Yes — I'll convert acceptance criteria into a short checklist and share here.
deploy-bot: scheduled: ci/canary-model-onboard-job #342 started by marc_eng at 2187654700
marc_eng: FYI I kicked off a kernel branch: github.com/redwood-inference/srv-runtime/compare/sylvan-rotary-fix. Smoke logs: ```
[smoke] model: clearpay/sylvan-2-13b@f3a1c9 - loaded - fp16 - ok
[perf] p50: 210ms p95: 380ms @ 8rps
```
neha_ml: Preliminary int8 pass results: p50 230ms p95 410ms, quality delta ~1.8% on the supplied prompt subset. I'll run full suite once we get the full prompt set.
liam_infra: Reserved 2x A100 slots in eu-west for pilot window (pending ops confirmation). Added routing policy snippet to staging.
ricardo_devex: Drafted PR for docs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex/pull/514 — includes example config and SDK call.
anya: Great progress. Next steps: Sam to confirm legal fallback opt-in + send full prompt set. Engineering to finish kernel PR and full int8 eval. Infra to confirm reserved capacity. Product will create a concise checklist to share with customer.
sam_sales: I'll update thread when legal confirms. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
